headline: AMERICAS GOLD & SILVER HITS 1,062 g/t Ag IN NEW GALENA VEIN — CRESCENT DRILLING RETURNS 1,891 g/t Ag
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver Corporation (TSX: USA) announced September 18 the first results from its largest-ever exploration program at the Galena Complex in Idaho's Coeur d'Alene silver district: a new vein discovery on the operating 49 level (49-817) grading 1,062 g/t Ag, 0.7% Cu and 0.6% Sb over 1.2 metres, while the adjacent Crescent Mine delivered 1,891 g/t Ag, 0.3% Cu over 1.3 metres and 1,560 g/t Ag, 0.3% Cu over 1.1 metres from separate vein structures — grades that significantly exceed the current modelled Mineral Resource for both mines; management notes that infill intercepts are regularly returning higher silver grades than the existing resource model, setting up an upward revision in the next MRE update; this is the company's largest-ever drill campaign across the Galena, Coeur and Crescent mines, with more assays expected in coming weeks from a program targeting resource conversion and new discovery simultaneously.

headline: TUDOR GOLD HITS 44 g/t Au AT SURFACE NEAR TREATY CREEK'S PERFECTSTORM — EPITHERMAL GOLD SYSTEM CONFIRMED ABOVE PORPHYRY
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSXV: TUD) reported September 17 results from ten drill holes at the Perfectstorm Zone of its 17,913-hectare Treaty Creek Project in BC's Golden Triangle, expanding the copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry system (the 'PSP Zone') while simultaneously confirming a near-surface gold-dominant epithermal system (the 'PSE Zone') sitting above and around the porphyry — a geological architecture that historically commands significantly higher valuations than a porphyry alone; surface sampling 1.2 kilometres northwest of current drilling returned grades up to 44.38 g/t gold, materially expanding the system's footprint; four near-surface follow-up holes have been drilled with assays pending, while two rigs remain active; Treaty Creek (80% Tudor, 20% Seabridge) neighbours Seabridge's KSM property to the southwest and Newmont's Brucejack Mine to the southeast — arguably the most mineralized corridor in the district.

headline: U.S. DFC APPROVES US$414M FOR NIGER'S DASA URANIUM MINE — EXPORT ROUTE THE LAST HURDLE BEFORE CONSTRUCTION
snippet: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) Board approved a debt facility of up to US$414.2 million for Global Atomic Corporation's Dasa Uranium Project in Niger, West Africa on September 16-17, 2026 — structured as a US$397.4 million term loan plus a US$16.8 million cost overrun facility, making it the largest US government financing commitment to an African uranium project in the current cycle; Dasa is Africa's largest and highest-grade uranium mine, targeting commercial production in H2 2028 with underground development already complete to the ore zone and 11% of life-of-mine production covered by offtake agreements; the financing is conditional on establishing a viable yellowcake export route — complicated by Niger's 2023 military coup that expelled French state-backed miner Orano and strained Niger's relationship with neighbouring transit states; the DFC commitment is widely read as a diplomatic signal of US re-engagement with Niamey two years after the coup and a direct counter to France's supply-chain influence in African uranium.

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD DECLARES COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION AT HAMMERDOWN — NEWFOUNDLAND MINE TARGETS 25,000 oz/yr AT US$2,500 AISC
snippet: New Found Gold Corp. (TSX: NFGC) declared commercial production at its Hammerdown Gold Mine in central Newfoundland on September 16, 2026 — confirming a milestone reached operationally on August 19 after the Pine Cove Mill sustained throughput, recovery, and feed grade metrics above PEA thresholds over a continuous 60-day test period; Hammerdown produced 9,140 ounces of gold in the first eight months of 2026 at average realized prices of C$6,271 per ounce, and management guides for a run rate of 20,000-25,000 ounces per year at an all-in sustaining cost near US$2,500 per ounce; the milestone marks New Found Gold's transition from explorer to operating producer while the company simultaneously advances its larger Queensway flagship project, where an updated Mineral Resource Estimate and Technical Report are targeted for H2 2026; zero lost-time incidents over 262,000 person-hours and a 90%+ local Newfoundland workforce add a community-relation quality the market has increasingly priced into junior-to-mid-tier transitions.

headline: HEENEY CAPITAL WINS 30-YEAR VENEZUELA GOLD CONCESSION — $1B DEAL WITH MERCURIA BRINGS CHOCO MINE PRODUCTION TO U.S.
snippet: U.S. investment firm Heeney Capital and commodities trader Mercuria Energy secured a 30-year concession to operate Venezuela's Choco gold mine in El Callao, Bolivar state — announced at the G20 energy ministerial in Houston on September 16, 2026 — with initial investment of up to $1 billion planned to restore and expand production and direct output to U.S. buyers; the deal adds to Heeney and Mercuria's earlier May 2026 framework covering Venezuelan minerals, aluminum and gold with a combined annual export value estimated at $2.2 billion; for junior miners, the deal is a macro signal: if Western capital can now operate at scale in Venezuela, the geopolitical risk premiums applied to South American exploration assets that had previously closed that market to Western operators may begin to normalize; it also confirms that US policy is actively diversifying critical metal and gold supply chains away from China and French-aligned producers simultaneously.

headline: TROILUS MINING DRILLS 3.38 g/t AuEq OVER 22m INSIDE 129m CORRIDOR AT QUÉBEC GOLD-COPPER PROJECT
snippet: Troilus Mining Corp. (TSX: TLO) reported results from nine holes totalling 4,728 metres at the Z87 Pit optimization program at its Troilus Gold-Copper Project in north-central Québec: best intercept of 3.38 g/t AuEq over 22.05 metres within a 129.05-metre corridor averaging 0.95 g/t AuEq from the Inferred domain — a grade and width combination that supports upgrading this block to Indicated confidence ahead of the project's planned feasibility study update; Troilus sits within a district previously operated by Inmet Mining as a bulk-tonnage copper-gold mine that produced 2 billion pounds of copper and 4.3 million ounces of gold before closing in 1996, supporting the district's metallurgical track record; the project hosts 11.7 million ounces AuEq in the M&I category, positioning it as one of Québec's larger undeveloped gold-copper resources and a logical takeout target in the current M&A environment.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,380 AFTER FED HIKE — RECORD 289t CENTRAL BANK BUYING IN Q2 IS THE REAL FLOOR SIGNAL
snippet: GoldSilver.com's post-Fed gold outlook argues that the market's fixation on the September 15-16 rate hike is misplaced: gold held near $4,380 after the decision — far above price levels at equivalent tightening moments in prior cycles — because the structural demand underpinning this bull market is central bank buying, not speculative flows; central banks purchased a record 288.9 tonnes in Q2 2026, up 62% year-over-year, during a quarter when the gold price fell 16%, demonstrating that sovereign buyers treat price dips as accumulation opportunities; the analysis maintains that bank consensus targets ($4,500–$5,200) remain unchanged, the September 24 Trump-Xi summit outcome is the next binary catalyst, and the correct read on the rate hike is that it confirms the Fed is near the end of the cycle — historically a tailwind for gold, not a headwind.

headline: SILVER ABSORBED THE HIKE AT $66.51 — SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT OF 46.3MOZ AND POSITIONING STILL NOT CROWDED
snippet: GoldSilver.com's post-hike silver analysis frames the rate decision as already priced in by the market, while the physical supply deficit remains chronically under-owned: silver finished September 18 at $66.51 per ounce after absorbing the Federal Reserve's rate increase with a modest intraday pullback before recovering, supported by a structural supply deficit forecast at 46.3 million ounces for 2026 — the sixth consecutive annual shortfall — and a cumulative drawdown of above-ground stocks since 2021 totalling 762.1 million ounces; managed-money net long positions remain thin at approximately 13,000 contracts per the September 18 COT report, well below levels recorded when silver hit its January all-time high near $121 per ounce, suggesting the speculative trade is not yet crowded; the analysis projects silver trading above $100 per ounce on a resumption of the structural uptrend, with the $75-76 range identified as the next key technical test.

headline: RECORD $3,076/oz GOLD MARGIN IN Q1 — BUT SLIDING-SCALE ROYALTIES AND DIESEL COSTS ARE EATING PRODUCER UPSIDE
snippet: Discovery Alert's September 2026 analysis documents the growing gap between headline gold mining margins — a record US$3,076 per ounce all-in sustaining cost margin in Q1 2026, up 134% year-over-year — and what actually flows to shareholders: government royalties on a sliding-scale basis in key jurisdictions mean that a 10% rise in gold price does not produce a 10% improvement in net cash flow because the state's share accelerates faster near the top brackets; producers with heavy diesel exposure and operations in jurisdictions near their royalty cap face margin compression that does not show up in simple AISC calculations; the piece identifies the structural characteristics separating genuinely margin-resilient producers from those whose numbers look good on paper but are constrained by structure — jurisdiction, energy supply type, and whether local-currency revenues offset operating-cost inflation — providing a practical framework for evaluating producers versus royalty streamers at $4,400 gold.

headline: NICOLA MINING BEGINS 800m SILVER DRILL AT BC'S TREASURE MOUNTAIN — MB ZONE TARGETING HIGH-GRADE EXTENSIONS
snippet: Nicola Mining Inc. (NASDAQ: NICM; TSXV: NIM) commenced its 2026 exploration drilling program September 18 at the Treasure Mountain silver-gold property approximately 30 kilometres northeast of Hope, British Columbia — a historic high-grade silver producer in the province's silver-copper belt — with a four-hole, approximately 800-metre program targeting the MB Zone where the highest historical silver grades were mined at surface and in early underground development; assay results are expected by year-end and will be used to refine the geological model for underground potential; the program is small in scope but strategically timed: BC high-grade silver veins near infrastructure are among the assets attracting renewed mid-tier M&A attention as silver's sixth consecutive structural supply deficit narrows the discount historically applied to primary silver exploration projects.
